top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, KLOwen, Lightforce, SmartSTL, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, damon ultima brackets, SLB, Aliwell
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, rentability, staff efficiency, diary changes, practice optimisation, emergencies decrease, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in second and third order movements
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually save them time or money, or that it will meaningfully reduce appointments or chair time. They want proof that DM delivers measurable efficiency and financial benefits, especially for braces and aligner cases, and are concerned about the real-world impact on their workflow and bottom line.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, video links, recent studies, only Australian studies, only German studies, only academic publication, only German language
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
Are Damon brackets more efficient than other brands?
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, region-specific, and product-specific ROI and efficiency data, especially for non-Invisalign appliances and multi-location or large practices. Comparative studies and real-world financial outcomes are most lacking.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnostics
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, accuracy of scanning, occlusal assessment, class I goal, FDA application, AI versus orthodontist, accuracy in detecting malocclusions, accuracy in remote monitoring, accuracy with aligner unseats, accuracy of smartphone-based monitoring
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI and SmartSTL are accurate enough for clinical decision-making, especially compared to in-person assessment or other digital tools. They are concerned about false positives/negatives, regulatory validation, and whether AI can match or exceed orthodontist judgment.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, peer-reviewed, white paper, clinical study, FDA data, only academic publication
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application
How accurate is SmartSTL AI

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct head-to-head accuracy studies versus orthodontists and regulatory-grade validation data are limited. More peer-reviewed, quantitative accuracy studies—especially for SmartSTL and new AI features—are needed.
